Numismatic Report: The 2006-P Jefferson Nickel is part of the 'Westward Journey' series, specifically representing the 'Return to Monticello' design. For 2006, the reverse design reverted to a modified version of the classic Monticello, but with a more detailed and aesthetically pleasing rendition by Felix Schlag's original design. The obverse also saw a significant change, featuring a new, forward-facing portrait of Thomas Jefferson, designed by Jamie Franki, replacing the long-standing profile portrait. With high mintages from the Philadelphia Mint, the 2006-P nickel in uncirculated condition is still quite common and primarily collected by those completing a series or appreciating the updated designs.

Numismatic Report: The 1964 Jefferson Nickel represents a standard issue of the series, which began in 1938. Designed by Felix Schlag, the obverse features a portrait of Thomas Jefferson, while the reverse depicts his Virginia home, Monticello. The year 1964 is notable as it was the last year for 90% silver dimes, quarters, and half dollars before the introduction of clad coinage, although the nickel's composition had already reverted to 75% copper and 25% nickel after the wartime silver issues. Millions of 1964 nickels were minted, with the Philadelphia Mint (no mint mark) producing a vast quantity (over 1 billion), making them very common. Due to their high mintage and non-precious metal composition, average circulated examples typically hold a value only slightly above face value, primarily as collector's items for completing sets or as educational pieces about mid-20th century U.S. coinage.
